articles.title: Evaluation of Radiograph Parameters Used to Assess Prosthetic Overlengthening in Radial Head Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Welsch J, Bollepalli H, Choudhury A, Van Boxtel M, Qawasmi F, Valiquette A, et al.
articles.population: Cadaver upper extremities with radial head prosthetics implanted at varying lengths
articles.sample_size: 4 fellowship-trained upper extremity orthopaedic surgeons evaluating radiographs
articles.outcomes: Inter-rater and intra-rater reliability of two radiographic landmarks (lateral ulnohumeral joint space and proximal edge of lesser sigmoid notch) for assessing prosthetic overlengthening
articles.take_home: Neither radiographic measurement was sufficiently reliable on its own to accurately assess whether a radial head replacement was too long. Surgeons need to use multiple assessment methods and ensure proper elbow positioning when checking radiographs after this operation.

articles.title: Assistant Experience Enhances the Learning Curve in Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Comparative CUSUM Analysis of Three Surgeons.
articles.authors: Taniguchi S, Hirakawa Y, Manaka T, Nakazawa K, Ito Y, Terai H
articles.population: Shoulder surgeons performing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: Three surgeons, 60 consecutive cases each (180 cases total)
articles.outcomes: Operative time, intraoperative blood loss, and intraoperative and postoperative complications
articles.take_home: Surgeons who had prior experience as assistants under experienced surgeons learned reverse total shoulder replacement faster and safer, achieving stable operative times and lower blood loss earlier than surgeons without assistant experience. Complications were more common during early learning and decreased once surgeons became proficient.

articles.title: Prediction of Acromial and Scapular Spine Fractures After Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty using Machine Learning: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Schneller T, Cina A, Maggini E, Klimov A, Braun M, Pfender A, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using machine learning
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Incidence and prediction of acromial and scapular spine fractures after surgery; model sensitivity 0.71, specificity 0.61, AUROC 0.71
articles.take_home: A machine learning model can help identify patients at higher risk of fractures to the shoulder blade after reverse shoulder replacement surgery. Risk factors include certain implant designs, rotator cuff tear arthropathy, older age and osteoporosis.

articles.title: Simultaneous versus Staged Bilateral Shoulder Replacement: A Matched Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Pina G, Lacouture JD, Shi B, Boileau P
articles.population: Patients undergoing bilateral shoulder replacement for osteoarthritis, cuff tear arthropathy, avascular necrosis, or rheumatoid arthritis
articles.sample_size: 16 simultaneous bilateral patients (32 shoulders) matched to 32 staged bilateral patients (64 shoulders)
articles.outcomes: Length of hospital stay, complications, reoperation rate, range of motion, Constant score, and Subjective Shoulder Value
articles.take_home: In carefully selected patients aged 80 years or under with good health status and social support, having both shoulder replacements at the same time reduces hospital stay compared to staged surgery, whilst achieving the same clinical results and patient satisfaction. No serious complications occurred in either group.

articles.title: The Humeral Bone Loss (HUMBL) Classification Identifies Patterns of Humeral Bone Loss Associated with Various Revision, Instability, and Humeral Loosening Rates in Primary and Revision Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Nieboer M, Cardona H, Vasquez-Lloret A, Macfarlane A, Narain A, Barlow J, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary or revision shoulder arthroplasty with humeral bone loss
articles.outcomes: All-cause reoperation rate, postoperative instability rate, and humeral loosening rate stratified by bone loss pattern
articles.take_home: More severe patterns of humeral bone loss are associated with higher rates of needing further surgery, shoulder instability, and implant loosening. Ectatic bone loss (expansion of the bone cortex) was found to carry particularly high complication rates.

articles.title: Effect of prior rotator cuff repair technique and timing on clinical outcomes of reverse shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Holt KE, Hao KA, Bindi VE, Kaiser AHA, Hones KM, Wright JO, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study from prospectively collected database
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse shoulder arthroplasty after prior rotator cuff repair for non-tumour and non-fracture indications
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, forward elevation, and external rotation at mean 4.8 years follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients who had arthroscopic rotator cuff repair before their shoulder replacement, or who had a longer gap between the two operations, achieved better results after reverse shoulder arthroplasty. Those with prior arthroscopic repair had better pain scores and shoulder movement compared to those who had open repair.

articles.title: The management of distal humeral fractures in older patients.
articles.authors: Yoong AWH, Super JT, Tan GJS, Watts AC, Ollivere BJ, Duckworth AD
articles.population: Older adults with distal humeral fractures
articles.outcomes: Functional outcomes, reoperation rates, infection, nonunion, instability, loosening
articles.take_home: Treatment options for broken bones at the bottom of the upper arm in older people include non-operative care, surgery to fix the bone with plates and screws, or replacement of the elbow joint. Recent studies show that elbow replacement and surgical fixation give similar short to medium-term results, though surgery to fix the bone may need more repeat operations.

articles.title: Time-course changes in bone mineral density after anatomical and reverse total shoulder arthroplasty : a dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-based study.
articles.authors: Nakazawa K, Manaka T, Ito Y, Hirakawa Y, Nishiura R, Oi N, et al.
articles.study_type: Longitudinal observational study using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry
articles.population: Patients undergoing anatomical total shoulder arthroplasty or reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 94 reverse total shoulder arthroplasties and 43 anatomical total shoulder arthroplasties
articles.outcomes: Bone mineral density changes around the humeral component at three weeks, six months, one year, and two years postoperatively; association between bone loss, osteoporosis, and clinical shoulder function scores
articles.take_home: After reverse shoulder replacement, bone density decreases over time in certain areas around the implant, particularly in patients with osteoporosis, which may be associated with poorer shoulder function. Patients with osteoporosis undergoing reverse shoulder replacement may need closer follow-up and better osteoporosis management.

articles.title: Preoperative thoracic kyphosis influences clinical outcomes and joint range of motion after reverse shoulder arthroplasty: A retrospective study from the FP-UCBM shoulder study group.
articles.authors: Franceschetti E, Gregori P, Bruna M, Russo F, Giurazza G, Tanzilli A, et al.
articles.outcomes: Shoulder flexion, abduction, constant score, visual analogue scale pain, simple shoulder test, and SANE score
articles.take_home: Patients with severe thoracic kyphosis (Cobb angle 47 degrees or more) had less shoulder movement in flexion and abduction, and lower functional scores after reverse shoulder arthroplasty compared to those with less kyphosis. Spinal curvature may affect how well the shoulder works after surgery.
